review.intro: Morning update, revised after your decisions: we keep the original ('stuck-start') y-polarized branches as the main data and run ONE side calibration to measure how much the stuck start matters. Each item opens the exact cut in the Cuts view (panels M_z / E/N / <A_v>,<B_p>; filled = up branch, hollow = dn branch).

items.title: 1. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.5 — clean first-order jump
items.text: M_z jumps at h_z ~ 0.375 with a hysteresis loop (~0.25-0.5): the up branch rises steeply between 0.40 and 0.50, the dn branch drops between 0.35 and 0.25.

items.title: 2. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.4 — calibration done: stuck start does NOT move the jump (0.325 either way)
items.text: Main branches: jump 0.325, loop ~0.15-0.35; the up branch started stuck. CALIBRATION (side folder, COMPLETE 14/14; 0.65-0.70 merged with both branches): a second up chain started from the dn branch's good y-pol state lies 5.0-2.4 below the stuck up branch at h_z 0.25-0.30, stays y-polarized to 0.40 (M_z 0.41), then jumps over 0.40 -> 0.45 (M_z 0.41 -> 0.66) and merges with both branches by 0.50 (E within 0.3, M_z within 0.01). It does NOT retrace the dn curve: it opens a WIDER loop (0.15-0.45). Lowest-energy curve with it: rt below dn up to 0.30, dn lower from 0.35 (rt - dn = -2.39 / +0.19), so the jump is still 0.325. Net energy crossing 0.345. Conclusion: the stuck start costs energy on the y-pol side and narrows the loop, but leaves the transition location unchanged within one grid step, as you expected.

items.title: 3. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.6 — loop narrowing
items.text: Jump ~0.475; the up/dn gap is smaller than at 1.4-1.5.

items.title: 4. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.7 — marginal
items.text: M_z rises steeply around 0.5 but the up/dn gap is small; locator 0.525, not flagged 'ok'.

items.title: 5. z<->y at h_x = 0, h_y = 1.8 — crossover (line has ended)
items.text: Both branches follow one M_z curve. They differ only in energy, which is the stuck-anchor effect, not hysteresis. So the z<->y line ends between h_y 1.7 and 1.8 (L = 4).

items.title: 6. z<->y at h_x = 0.2, h_y = 1.4 — jump shifted up by 0.05
items.text: Jump 0.375 (h_x = 0: 0.325). Loop ~0.20-0.45: up jumps between 0.40 and 0.45, dn drops between 0.25 and 0.20. Its up start is stuck by the <B_p> fingerprint but heals within 1-2 points (up is only ~0.3 above dn at h_z = 0.1), so it does not affect the jump.

items.title: 7. z<->y at h_x = 0.2, h_y = 1.5 — also +0.05
items.text: Jump 0.425 (h_x = 0: 0.375). Loop ~0.30-0.45. Up start stuck but heals quickly (as in item 6).

items.title: 8. z<->y at h_x = 0.5, h_y = 1.4 — first-order jump at 0.425 (+0.10 vs h_x = 0)
items.text: Both branches complete. Jump 0.425 +- 0.025 (ok), hysteresis loop 0.25-0.55: up (from y-pol) jumps between 0.45 and 0.55 (M_z 0.43 -> 0.72), dn (from z-pol) stays z-polarized down to 0.35 (M_z 0.49 vs up 0.25) and drops between 0.35 and 0.25. Net energy crossing ~0.43-0.47 (dn lower at 0.45/0.50, merged within 0.1 above 0.55). Trend of the z<->y line at h_y = 1.4: 0.325 / 0.375 / 0.425 at h_x = 0 / 0.2 / 0.5 -- the shift at h_x = 0.5 is +0.10, a bit less than your +0.15 guess.

items.title: 9. x<->y at h_z = 0, h_y = 1.3 — crossover (your in-plane-sweep test)
items.text: No jump and no hysteresis: up and dn agree to |dM_x| ~0.01 from h_x 0.75 to 1.25 and M_x rises smoothly. The x<->y line therefore ends between the pocket tip (h_y ~1.19) and 1.3. (The up start at h_x = 0.4 was stuck but had healed by h_x ~0.75, where the branches agree.)

items.title: 10. x<->y at h_z = 0, h_y = 1.4 — crossover (dn restarted and landing)
items.text: Up branch complete and smooth. The dn branch (restarted after a W&B logging crash) has reached h_x 1.15 and lies on the up curve (|dM_x| <= 0.002, dn lower by 0.1-0.3): merged, no jump, no loop, same as h_y = 1.3 -> crossover.

items.title: 11. h_x = 0.2, h_z = 0.15 — reclassified: trivial <-> trivial, not roof
items.text: S2 on the up branch falls from 2.0 to 0.7 between h_y 0.8 and 1.2, i.e. the chain turns trivial through the 2nd-order edge BEFORE the jump at 1.225, so that jump is z-pol <-> y-pol (hollow square, dashed line). The h_x = 0.2 roof is h_z = 0 (1.185) and 0.1 (1.175) only, and its tip sits lower than the h_x = 0 tip.

items.title: 12. h_x = 0.2, h_z = 0.2 — also trivial <-> trivial
items.text: Same as (0, 0.2): S2 is already below 1 at h_y ~1.0, so the 1.225 jump is a z-pol <-> y-pol point, not roof.

items.title: 13. The h_x = 0 'tip' (h_z = 0.15) — kept as measured
items.text: Roof 1.245 with a stuck dn start. The anchor-recipe trials were cancelled (decision: roll with stuck starts); the h_y = 1.4 calibration (item 2) will tell whether the stuck start biases jump locations.

items.title: 14. All three h_x planes overlaid
items.text: Phase diagram -> '(h_y, h_z) planes at fixed h_x'.

items.title: 15. 3D: roof points joined across the h_x planes
items.text: In the 3D panel the topological -> trivial roof points at equal h_z are now joined across h_x = 0 / 0.2 / 0.5 (solid red; h_z = 0 and 0.1 have roof points in all three planes). Each h_x plane also has its own meridian (indigo / pink / teal).

items.title: 16. z<->y at h_x = 0.5, h_y = 1.5 — rounded: hysteresis band but no sharp step
items.text: Up rises smoothly (M_z 0.30 -> 0.69 over h_z 0.40-0.60, steepest 0.50-0.55). Dn, coming down, stays more z-polarized (M_z 0.44 vs 0.30 at 0.40, 0.63 vs 0.46 at 0.50), so a hysteresis band shows over 0.40-0.65. But dn lies ABOVE up in energy everywhere (by 2.1 at 0.40 down to 0.2 at 0.65), with no energy crossing and no step >= 0.2. Winner curve = up, centred ~0.525. This looks like h_x = 0 at h_y 1.6-1.7 (marginal): the z<->y line weakens at h_x = 0.5 already at h_y = 1.5. No phase-diagram point yet (first-order electric cuts need an ok jump). Dn continues to 0.25.

items.title: 17. x<->y tip sweeps (h_z = 0): h_y 1.05-1.2 cross the POCKET EDGE, not an x<->y line
items.text: Up branches start ON the 3 ln 2 plateau (S2 = 2.02 / 2.07 / 2.10 / 2.12 at h_y 1.05 / 1.1 / 1.15 / 1.2) to h_x 0.60-0.65, then M_x jumps over 0.65 -> 0.70 with S2 -> 0.8-1.55. Jump 0.675 +- 0.025 at 1.1/1.15/1.2 (0.625, not sharp, at 1.05). This is the topological -> trivial MAGNETIC EDGE, flat in h_y 1.0-1.2, so the pocket tip at h_z = 0 is at h_y >= 1.2. Overlap h_x 0.75-0.95 (dn now down to 0.75-0.80): dn is LOWER than up by 2.3-2.9 (h_y 1.05), 1.3-5.8 (1.1) and 6.8-7.3 (1.15). Dn is canted (M_y 0.37-0.45 vs 0.23 on up; B_p 0.15 vs 0.26-0.30; S2 0.13-0.35). So the post-jump up states are metastable (they keep topological memory). Along dn, M_x and M_y vary smoothly, with no second jump: still no x<->y line at h_y 1.05-1.2. The edge's true location = the up/dn energy crossing once dn reaches 0.60-0.65 (at h_y = 1.0 that gave 0.622, same as the jump). Dn is 2-7 lower at 0.75, so the crossing may sit below the 0.675 jump. Notes: h_y = 1.05 dn at 0.95 is an outlier (E +8; spurious crossing 0.911, unused). The h_y = 1.2 dn anchor is re-running (58848725, healthy). For you: (1.05-1.2, 0) are registered as trivial<->trivial (MAGNETIC_JUMP_PRIMARY) and drawn that way, but S2 says topological -> trivial. Relabel?

items.title: 18. h_y = 1.0, h_z = 0 magnetic cut: dn extended to 0.5 — wide hysteresis, E crossing 0.62
items.text: The dn (x-pol) branch, extended 0.70 -> 0.50, stays x-polarized all the way (M_x 0.81-0.85, S2 0.20-0.25) while up stays topological to ~0.7. It does NOT rejoin the up branch: a clean first-order loop 0.50-0.75. Net energy crossing at h_x = 0.622 +- 0.015 (E_dn - E_up = +7.8 / +4.3 / +1.1 / -1.4 / -3.5 at 0.50-0.70); jump locator 0.625 ok.
